analysis:
Only base text and a truncated patch excerpt were supplied for provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift; the head-side code was not visible beyond the excerpt.

The changed ranges in the excerpt are the reclaimableMemoryBytes accounting around base lines 1309-1313 and evictUntilAvailable around base lines 1332-1345. The patch adds CBv2RetainedKVSegments.retainedBytes to the reclaimable-memory total. It adds releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad(), which calls GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments() and then clearCacheAfterConfirmedNativeOwnership(). It also adds a poolDropped flag in evictUntilAvailable and touches the fastAdmissionReject cache-clear call sites (base lines 1382 and 1515).

Security relevance is limited. These are availability and admission-heuristic changes. They affect TB-007 and the T-028 residual-GPU-memory concerns, and could marginally affect DoS-related availability. Releasing retained KV segments and clearing MLX cache moves toward reducing residual inference data, not increasing it.

I saw no change to the weight-hash TOCTOU guard (base lines 597-641), the SSD prefix-cache gating, T-041 cache scoping or TTL, encryption, or authorization. No plaintext exposure or new trust-boundary crossing was identified.

Remaining questions for integration:
- Whether GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments and busyEnginesKeepReclaimableMemory (defined in other files) are safe under concurrent engine steps.
- Whether the reclaim-before-evict loop can be driven by remote requests into repeated cache drops that degrade performance. This is a minor availability concern and is unverified from the supplied evidence.
- Whether a stale, un-zeroed KV segment could be reused across requests. That is outside the supplied evidence.
